title: Paris demonstrators clash with police over living costs and public services
seoTitle: Paris protests over living costs and services

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the rising cost of living, declining purchasing power, poor school conditions, and public services.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand relief from economic hardship, better public services, and improved education conditions.
tea.changed: Oct 19: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced partial curfews as unrest continued in several urban centres.

summary: Demonstrations over living costs, declining purchasing power, and public services broke out across France, leading to widespread clashes with police, property damage, and looting in Paris and other cities. The unrest originated from weeks of student protests over school conditions and teacher shortages, expanding into broader grievances ahead of the presidential election. Authorities reported hundreds of arrests and multiple injuries among security forces as rioters targeted commercial establishments and public buildings. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, warning of legal consequences for those involved, while local officials implemented emergency curfews to curb further disorder.
response: According to French authorities, police deployed tear gas and water cannons, and made numerous arrests. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, warning of legal action, while local authorities announced overnight curfews.

crowd.text: approximately 550,000 people participated in the protests, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez

injuries.text: more than 150 police officers were injured

updates.text: Protests and clashes broke out across Paris and multiple other French cities over living costs and public services.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu called for partial local curfews as unrest continued across urban centres.
